subject: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned for the pilot: 

Summary of objectives
- Validate Redwood Dedicated latency and cost at Sparrow's typical Q&A and summarization load for the triage workflow.
- Ensure token-level cost targets meet your procurement threshold for the pilot month.

Ask / data we need from you (one-pagers appreciated)
1) Representative traffic profile: RPS during business hours, expected peak bursts, average and 95th-percentile prompt lengths (tokens), typical output lengths.
2) Concurrency target (how many simultaneous sessions/users you expect).
3) Example request/response JSONs (sanitized) and any API call rate limiting on your side.

Proposed POC timeline (draft)
- Week 0: Traffic sample + success criteria (you)
- Week 1: Environment prep + ingest sample traffic (Redwood)
- Week 2: Baseline runs + tuning (Redwood + Sparrow)
- Week 3: Validation, readout, and next-step decision

Owners
- Alex (me): overall pilot coordination and SOW/contract points
- Sergio: technical onboarding, model/runtime config, load tests
- Marissa: customer success & acceptance confirmation

I'll spin up a shared folder for artifacts and drop a simple CSV template for traffic if that's helpful. If this looks correct, could you send the sample traffic file and any internal success thresholds (eg. P95 latency < 350ms, cost per 1k tokens <$X) by EOD Monday?

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast on this.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_poc_template.csv (attachment stub)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rebecca Shaw <r.shaw@sparrowhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching an export of one week's anonymized traffic and a short notes doc. High level answers below and I've attached sparrow_sample_traffic.csv.

Quick answers
- Typical daytime RPS: 6–12 RPS across the cluster; single-region peak observed at 28 RPS for short bursts (~90s) during morning syncs.
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Prompt tokens: median prompt ~80 tokens, 95th percentile ~420 tokens. Outputs: 60–350 tokens depending on request type.
- Tokenization: We primarily use UTF-8 plaintext; some messages include patient metadata which we've removed for this export.

Questions for Redwood
- Can you confirm if prefix caching would help given our repeat question patterns?
- What's your recommended target GPUs/config for this workload?

Attachment: sparrow_sample_traffic.csv (text/csv, 34KB)

Liam O'Connor
Head of Product — Clinical AI
Sparrow Health
liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-29T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification

Thanks Liam — this is perfect and exactly what we need. I downloaded the CSV and started a quick pass for shape/variance. Two quick clarifications before we schedule baseline runs: 

1) Could you highlight which rows correspond to the triage workflow vs. the scheduled summarization jobs? They have different SLOs so we want to separate them in the load profile.
2) Any rate-limiting or backoff behavior from Sparrow's side that we should model for the client?

Sergio — can you take point on parsing the CSV and preparing an initial load plan? Goal: run a synthetic baseline that mirrors your indicated peaks (28 RPS bursts, 40 concurrent).

Marissa — looping you in for acceptance criteria capture. I've put a draft in the shared Drive: Sparrow_MVP_success_criteria.xlsx (will share link). Please add any business-level pass/fail items (eg. max cost target, acceptable error modes).

I'll propose a 30-minute kickoff for the baseline run on Monday at 10am PT if that works for your team.

— Alex
Attachment: Sparrow_MVP_success_criteria.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification

Morning team — adding a concise POC acceptance checklist so Sparrow's stakeholders have a clear view of what 'success' means for the pilot. I've pasted the key points below and added more detail in the Drive doc.

POC acceptance (draft)
- Latency: P95 end-to-end inference latency for triage < 350ms (measured at Redwood edge).
- Throughput: System must tolerate 28 RPS bursts with no more than 5% request failures.
- Concurrency: Maintain stable KV cache behavior for up to 50 concurrent sessions (we'll test up to 50 to build headroom).
- Quality: No regression on the provided eval set (we'll run a small prompt set and compare outputs to baseline).
- Cost: Pilot-month projected token cost within 15% of the estimate we provide after tuning.

Operational notes
- We'll instrument token-level billing breakdown and share daily dashboards during the pilot.
- On escalations: Alex is commercial lead; Sergio is technical lead; Marissa will own acceptance sign-off and runbook handover.

Data points we still need from Sparrow (to complete readiness)
- Clarify triage vs scheduled summarization flags in the CSV (Liam).
- Any internal rate limits/backoff logic.
- A sample of 'long prompt' messages (the 95th percentile) in sanitized JSON (to validate memory/window sizing).

Next steps
1) Liam to flag triage rows and share the sanitized long-prompt sample (by EOD Tue).
2) Sergio to submit the baseline test plan (by Wed).
3) Kickoff baseline run: proposed Mon 10am PT (confirm availability).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Sparrow_MVP_success_criteria.xlsx (shared link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4dSparrowPlaybook)

From: Rebecca Shaw <r.shaw@sparrowhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@sparrowhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Sparrow pilot intake & traffic qualification

Thanks all — appreciate the clarity. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- I'll flag the triage rows in the CSV and upload a sanitized long-prompt JSON (should be in the Drive by EOD today).
- We can support a Monday 10am PT kickoff for the baseline; will have our infra engineer on the call.
- Regarding prefix caching: we have a high degree of repeat question phrasing in triage; if Redwood supports prefix/KV caching that respects privacy constraints, that could materially reduce cost — we'd like to see that in the tuning pass.

Question for Redwood (procurement check)
- If the pilot meets acceptance, what's the typical lead time and pricing cadence to convert to Dedicated reserved capacity? We may need that in the final readout.

I'll also upload a short doc that lists any internal compliance constraints for data handling during the pilot.

Regards,
Rebecca Shaw
VP, Clinical Operations | Sparrow Health
r.shaw@sparrowhealth.com
